text:
Ivy Chen: Heads up — since the east2 GPU scale-up this morning we've seen remote_write p95 and a spike in 5xx from the proxy to cortex :warning:
Raj Patel: saw that. any obvious correlation with scrape cardinality? :eyes:
Ivy Chen: yes, grafana shows a sudden ~15x increase in series from a handful of tenant namespaces that started running distributed profiling jobs. series keys include ephemeral labels like job_id and run_id
Sam Lee: are those labels being relabeled/dropped? sounds like cardinality gone wild
Ivy Chen: We suspected relabeling drift. Our prom relabel config for the exporter looks like this:
```
- source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_job_id]
  target_label: job_id
- source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_run_id]
  target_label: run_id
```
They recently added the profiling exporter which includes dynamic ids
Alex Gomez: immediate mitigation: drop those dynamic labels at scrape to avoid remote_write fanout. e.g. relabel to regex: .* -> "" or replace to "unknown"
Jordan Park: Also the remote_write batch size and queue config matter. We have small batch_size and limited queue_capacity for the proxy, so the burst from these tenants is overflowing and causing 504/502 from cortex proxy
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0312-17 - remote_write proxy 5xx spike (linked)
Raj Patel: proposal — two part: 1) emergency relabel rule to drop job_id/run_id for affected namespaces, 2) throttle tenant using per-tenant routing (route to slower ingestion or backoff) while we investigate
Ivy Chen: I can push a hotfix relabel in staging and then to prod. Suggested relabel snippet:
```
- action: replace
  source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_namespace]
  regex: "(profiling-tenant|sandbox-.*)"
  replacement: ""
  target_label: run_id
- action: replace
  source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_namespace]
  regex: "(profiling-tenant|sandbox-.*)"
  replacement: ""
  target_label: job_id
```
Sam Lee: while Ivy rolls that, ops: could we increase remote_write queue_capacity and max_shards temporarily? will buy time but cost CPU/memory
Alex Gomez: yes but watch GPU provisioning windows — the scale up churn earlier also caused kube-proxy conn resets which amplified the issue. If we increase queue too much we risk longer tail latency and more memory on proxies
Jordan Park: I'll patch the proxy config to increase max_pending_enqueue_time and backoff, and add a quick grafana panel to track queue backlog and per-tenant series delta
Ivy Chen: hotfix deployed to Canaries (profiling namespaces): relabels applied, monitoring now shows series delta falling back to baseline :thumbsup:
Raj Patel: good. follow-ups: 1) add validation on exporter to refuse dynamic id labels by default, 2) tune alert thresholds for remote_write 5xx to avoid paging on small blips, 3) run a spike test in staging to measure queue headroom
Sam Lee: add an alert that triggers on per-namespace series growth rate > 300% over 5m to catch future runaway exporters
Alex Gomez: also add a scheduled job to run relabel-sanity checks against new deployments in the CI pipeline
Ivy Chen: creating runbook notes and linking to the incident. Thanks everyone.
Jordan Park: leaving the incident open until we've got a postmortem and the exporter fix scheduled next sprint
Raj Patel: noted, will own PM for exporter validation. closing slack thread for now, move discussion to the incident doc for follow-ups :white_check_mark:
